title: ParvaGPU: Efficient Spatial GPU Sharing for Large-Scale DNN Inference in Cloud Environments
problem: GPU-based DNN inference servers in cloud environments must meet diverse Service Level Objective (SLO) latency requirements while minimizing resource consumption. Current approaches suffer from underutilization within GPU space partitions and external fragmentation when combining spatial and temporal sharing technologies.
motivation: Efficient GPU sharing in cloud inference reduces infrastructure costs while maintaining strict latency guarantees for multiple concurrent workloads.
method: ParvaGPU integrates NVIDIA's Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) for spatial partitioning and Multi-Process Service (MPS) for temporal multiplexing to enable combined sharing. The system addresses fragmentation and underutilization challenges by intelligently managing resource allocation across both partitioning dimensions. Evaluation on A100 GPUs with 11 diverse DNN workloads demonstrates SLO compliance and GPU usage reduction.
key_novelty: Unified integration of MIG spatial partitioning and MPS temporal multiplexing to simultaneously minimize internal underutilization and external fragmentation in GPU sharing.
contributions: Integration framework combining MIG and MPS for improved GPU utilization in inference workloads
Solution to minimize underutilization within space partitions
Approach to reduce external fragmentation in mixed MIG-MPS environments
Demonstration of SLO compliance with significant GPU usage reduction across diverse DNN workloads

metrics.speedup: Significant GPU usage reduction versus state-of-the-art

primary_theme: efficient GPU sharing for cloud inference
